overview.description: Durak ('Fool' in Russian) is Russia's most widely played card game. The goal is to NOT be the last player holding cardsâ€”the last player is the 'Durak' (Fool). Players attack with cards; the defender must beat each attacking card with a higher card of the same suit or any trump. If unable to defend, they take all attacked cards into their hand. A 36-card deck is used (6 through Ace). After each bout, players draw to replenish to 6 cards. The Podkidnoy (passing) variantâ€”where the attack can be redirected to the next playerâ€”is the standard form.

history.origins: One of Russia's oldest documented card games. References appear from at least the 18th century. It was the default family card game across the Soviet Union and remains the most ubiquitous Russian card game today.
timeline: Present: Most popular card game in Russia, Ukraine, and many post-Soviet states.
history.evolution: Two main variants: Prostoy Durak (simple defense, no passing) and Podkidnoy Durak (the attacker can 'throw in' additional matching-rank cards, and the attack can be 'redirected' by defender if a matching rank appears). Podkidnoy is the dominant modern form.
history.cultural: A Russian national treasure. The term 'Durak' (Fool) has cultural weightâ€”losing at Durak is a social embarrassment. The game is played across all age groups.

setup.players: Two to six players. Best with four playing in partnerships (two against two, partners opposite). Can also be played by two to six as individuals, or six in two teams of three sitting alternately. The player to the dealer's left is the first defender; the attacker sits to the defender's right.
setup.deck: 36 cards: Ranks 6-7-8-9-10-J-Q-K-A in each of 4 suits.
setup.dealing: 6 cards each. Turn one card as trump indicator; place under stock (suit visible). Stock face-down on top.

rules.objective: Shed all of your cards before the talon is exhausted and play ends. The game has no winner—only a loser: the last player left holding cards is the durak (fool) and loses the hand; in partnership play the team left with cards loses.
rules.gameplay: Attack with cards; defender beats or picks up. Refill to 6 from stock. Last with cards = Durak (loser).
keyRules: Cannot have more than 6 cards in your hand after a win. Refill back to 6 after each bout.
Once stock is empty, no more drawing. Play out remaining cards.
Last player with cards = Durak (Fool). Loser of the session.

strategy.basic: Attack with low cards (6s, 7s, 8s). Save trumps for defense or critical attacks. Never attack with a trump unless you need to.
strategy.intermediate: Card Counting: Track which trump ranks have been played. In Podkidnoy, use passing strategically to offload the attack to a player with fewer cards.
strategy.advanced: Endgame: Once the stock is empty, you know all remaining cards in the game. Calculate whether to attack aggressively to push remaining cards onto opponents or defend conservatively.
tips: Use 6s and 7s to throw in and exhaust the defender's good high cards.
Never pick up cards willingly unless the alternative is surrendering a trump.

difficulty.easy: Attacks with lowest card. Defends if possible.
difficulty.medium: Saves trump. Uses throw-in to exhaust defender. Considers card economy.
difficulty.hard: Full 36-card tracker. Perfect trump counting. Optimal throw-in timing. Endgame calculation of exact win probability.

considerations: Passing mechanic (Podkidnoy) creates multi-step attack chains.
Trump tracking is criticalâ€”exactly 9 trump cards in 36-card deck.
After stock empty, game becomes perfect information.
Attack card matching (rank must appear in active bout) requires careful bout state.

drawSources.notes: Replenish to 6 after each bout; attacker draws first, then other attackers clockwise, then defender. Face-up trump is drawn last.

trumpConfig.overtakingRule: Non-trump is beaten by higher same suit or any trump; trump only by higher trump.

validPlays.notes: Attack: play any card. Defend: beat with higher same suit or any trump. Throw-in: same rank as any card in current bout.

shedding.burnRules: Beaten cards and defender's cards are discarded from play when attack is beaten off.

edgeCases.text: Refill order after bout: attacker first, then other attackers in clockwise order, then defender.
Trump 6 may be exchanged for the face-up trump before talon is exhausted (by its holder only).
When stock is empty no more drawing; play continues until one player has all cards.
Maximum six attack cards per bout, or fewer if defender had fewer than six cards.
First hand: holder of lowest trump leads (may play any card). Subsequent hands: player to dealer's left leads.
Game can end in a draw when all players run out of cards in the same bout; previous loser deals again.

customActions.description: Deal six cards to each player face down, one at a time clockwise. Turn the next card face up for trump; place remaining cards face down on top of it crosswise so the trump suit stays visible (prikup/talon).
Play one card face up in front of the defender to start or continue an attack. Non-trump is beaten by a higher card of the same suit or any trump; trump only by a higher trump.
customActions.constraints: Attacker's turn; first attack may be any card; further attacks only with a card whose rank matches some card already in the current bout. Maximum six attack cards per bout (or defender's hand size if smaller).

customActions.description: Add another attack card whose rank matches any card already played in the current bout (attack or defence). Principal attacker has priority; other opponents may join with permission.
customActions.constraints: Only after defender has beaten the previous attack card. Same rank as some card in the bout; total attack cards not more than six or defender's hand size.

customActions.description: Decline to add more attack cards. In Perevodnoy variant, defender may instead transfer the attack to the next player by playing a card matching the attack rank.
customActions.constraints: Legal when it is your turn to attack or throw in and you choose not to play a card.

customActions.description: Beat an attack card by playing a higher card of the same suit or any trump from hand. Place the defending card on top of the attack card. No requirement to follow suit; trump may be used to beat non-trump.
customActions.constraints: Defender only. Card must be higher same suit or any trump (trump beats non-trump; higher trump beats lower trump).

customActions.description: Pick up all attack cards and any cards already played to beat them into your hand. Attack succeeds; you do not get the next attack. Other attackers may give you additional legal attack cards face up, which you also take.
customActions.constraints: Defender only, when unable or unwilling to beat the current attack card.

engine.deckDescription: A stripped French deck containing 36 cards with four suits (Hearts, Diamonds, Clubs, Spades) and nine ranks per suit (6 through Ace), created by removing cards 2 through 5 from a standard 52-card deck.
engine.suitDescription: Four traditional French suits: Hearts (Cœur), Diamonds (Carreau), Clubs (Trèfle), and Spades (Pique), each represented with standard French card design and distinct color coding for easy suit identification.
engine.rankDescription: Nine ranks per suit starting from 6: 6, 7, 8, 9, 10, Jack (Valet), Queen (Dame), King (Roi), and Ace as the highest card, where each rank has specific value and importance in determining game outcomes.
